proposed_facts.reason: Canonical clank code adds special-attribute x4 to copied Y without constraining its sign or magnitude. It calls the separate pillar constructor and returns true; that void constructor checks a nullable allocation. This supports replacing both 'slightly above' and guaranteed-creation wording.

The clank callback has no local guard or timer check, passes current owner, facing and adjusted position, and returns true unconditionally. The constructor makes one allocation request and handles failure internally without reporting success.

The damage-dealt callback likewise unconditionally passes current owner, facing and attribute-adjusted position to the separate pillar constructor. Its true return is independent of the constructor's nullable allocation outcome.
